title: CJS request-id fallback is declared but never used
reasoning: resolveToolCallRequestId accepts a fallbackId and routeToolCallToLocalRuntime passes event.id as that fallback, but the helper always returns an empty string when payload requestId/request_id is missing. The outer claim path also calls the helper without a fallback, so CJS tool-call events that rely on the event id as their only request identifier are rejected or cannot use the intended fallback.
reproduction: Send a CJS SDK tool-call event with payload.toolName set, no payload.requestId/request_id, and event.id set. routeSdkToolEventToLocalRuntime returns false because resolveToolCallRequestId ignores the fallback and returns an empty string.
recommendation: Either honor fallbackId in resolveToolCallRequestId when it is a non-empty string, and pass event.id in the claim check, or remove the fallback parameter and align callers so the request id contract is explicit.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and the dead fallback parameter indicates there is no coverage for event-id fallback behavior in the CJS routing path.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CJS coordinator test asserting whether an event.id-only tool call should be claimable. If supported, assert sendToolResult uses that id; if unsupported, assert the fallback parameter is removed from the implementation.
minimumFixScope: Clarify and align request id fallback handling in the CJS coordinator, with a focused regression test for the supported contract.
